1

  • N: izzizzū-ma | inappatū | qišta
  • T: They stood marvelling at the forest,
  • L: izzizzū-ma ← izuzzu I “to stand”; inappatū ← napātu I “to look at? jB(Gilg.)”; qišta ← qiāšu I “to give, present”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "V" 53

  • T: gazing at the lofty cedars,
  • L: ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; erēni ← erēnu I “cedar OAkk qišti e. cedar forest”; ittanaplasū ← naplāsu I “look, glance O/jB”; mēlâšu ← mēlû I “height, altitude Bab.”

4

  • N: ašar humbāba | ittallaku || šakin | kibsu
  • T: Where Ḫumbaba came and went there was a track,
  • L: ašar ← ašru III “pl. m. & f., place, site”; humbāba ← Humbaba I; ittallaku ← alāku I “to go”; šakin ← šakānu I “to put, place, lay down”; kibsu ← kibsu I “pl. m. & f. track, footprint”

5

  • N: harranātu | šutēšurā-ma || ṭubbat | girru
  • T: the paths were in good order and the way was well trodden.
  • L: harranātu ← harrānu I “f., later also m. way, road”; šutēšurā-ma ← šutēšuru I “(kept) in order jB”; ṭubbat ← ṭiābu I “to be(come) good”; girru ← gerru I “m. & f. way”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 OB "Harmal₂" 15

  • T: They were gazing at the Cedar Mountain,
  • L: immarū ← amāru I “to see”; šadâ ← šadû I “st. constr. šad(i)”; erēni ← erēnu I “cedar OAkk qišti e. cedar forest”

  • T: sweet was its shade, full of delight.

11

  • T: cedars and gum trees, [all entwined,] left no way in.
  • L: erēnu ← erēnu I “cedar OAkk qišti e. cedar forest”; ballukkum-ma ← ballukku I “(a tree) OAkk, Bab.”; nēreba ← nērebu I “entrance of house, land”; ul ← ul I “not Bab., to negate main clause”; īši ← išû I “to have (no pres., pret. īši, īšu”

12

  • N: [naši] | papalla || ana (ištēn) bēri | erēnu
  • T: For a league on all sides cedars [lifts up] saplings,
  • L: [naši] ← našû II “to lift, carry”; papalla ← papallu I “shoot, sprout j/NB”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; (ištēn) ← ištēn I “f. išteat, ištiat, iš/ltē/īt(um), iš/ltât, NA issēt”; bēri ← bēru III “double hour, league”; erēnu ← erēnu I “cedar OAkk qišti e. cedar forest”
  • Note: [RN1518: 70] suggests restoring naši, “lifts up,” at the beginning, after Palm and Vine 53′ (II.12): lammu ša ina rēš rāṭi našû papalla, “The almond tree, that lifts up its branches at the source of the ditch.”

  • T: cypresses [grew thick] for two-thirds of a league.
  • L: šurmēnu ← šurmēnu I “cypress as tree, timber”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; šinipât ← šinipu I “two-thirds (cf. GAG §70i) math. šinip šinipīya 2/3 of my 2/3 i.e.…”; bēr ← bēru III “double hour, league”
